description:
### US-018: Best-available seat selection
**As** a buyer, **I want** "best available N" to return contiguous seats honoring the map's
adjacency, atomically claimed. **Priority:** P2 **Depends on:** US-017
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A best-available request for N seats returns a contiguous run per the map's adjacency/rank
      data (TKT-3 provides both), claimed atomically in the same transaction that selected them —
      selection and claim never race.
- [ ] Contiguity relaxation rules are explicit and deterministic (e.g. split parties only when no
      contiguous run exists; never strand a single seat if the map forbids it — exact rules
      confirmed with the owner at Planning).
- [ ] Under the contention test, parallel best-available requests never double-assign and
      degrade fairly (no oversell, no deadlock, bounded retries).

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + unit + integration + smoke; mirrors CI)
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary (ADR-009 drift check)
- Money/ticket-path: audit-trail invariants hold (ADR-003)
- Read-endpoint changes: ADR-004 TTL tier declared with rationale

Parent epic: TKT-4. Full lineage: docs/product/prd-v1.md §TKT-4.

objective.note: Epic COS: best-available returns contiguous seats honoring map adjacency, claimed atomically.

scope.note: IN: best-available-N selection using TKT-3 adjacency/rank data, atomic select+claim, deterministic relaxation rules, parallel-request contention test. OUT: buyer-facing seat picker UI (TKT-35), pricing tiers in selection (TKT-5).

uncertainties.note: Relaxation rules (split parties, no stranded singles) confirmed with the owner at Planning — named in the ACs; algorithm choice is engineering.

dependencies.note: HARD blocker: US-017/TKT-80 (wired blocked-by) — needs seat claims to exist.

approach.note: Selection query over live seat availability + adjacency data inside the claim transaction; bounded retry on contention; determinism tested.

first_slice.note: Request best-available 4 on a half-sold row-ranked map → a contiguous run of 4, atomically held; parallel identical requests never overlap.

binding.rule: The inventory database is the sole write-side correctness boundary. Each mutation locks the inventory pool row first, then its claim rows; operations addressed by hold ID discover the pool with a non-locking read, then re-read the claim after locking the pool — every path has the same pool-to-claim lock order. A claim is held, confirmed, released, or expired; the last three are terminal. PostgreSQL time decides expiry: a transaction expires due holds before capacity accounting, so cleanup jobs are optional optimizations. Confirmed plus unexpired-held quantity may never exceed pool capacity. Hold creation requires an organizer-scoped idempotency key, single-use across the claim's full lifecycle. Reserved seats, date ranges, and entitlements reuse the lifecycle and lock ordering but add their own resource constraints.

governingAdrs.why: Selection and claim happen in one transaction under the pool lock — a select-then-claim race is the failure mode this ADR exists to prevent.
Best-available is a selection policy over seat claims, not a new claim kind.

reference.summary: PRD v1 §TKT-4 decomposition — the story text is the source of truth

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
Shaped at TKT-4 decomposition (2026-07-16). Classification: complex. All 8 DoR items met/deferred — claimable once prioritized (and blockers Done, where wired).

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 — promoted to Ready (owner, 2026-08-17)

**US-018: Best-available seat selection.**

Blocker satisfied: `blocked-by TKT-80` (US-017, seat-level claims) is **Done**, so the seat claims
this builds on exist.

⚠ **One thing to check at claim time, and it is not a DoR failure.** The ticket's AC says contiguity
comes from *"the map's adjacency/rank data (TKT-3 provides both)"* — and **TKT-3 is a Backlog
epic**. Its `dependencies` item is correctly `met`, because the wired blocker (TKT-80) is closed and
adjacency projection did ship via TKT-181. But whoever claims this should confirm the *rank* data it
wants actually exists before Planning, rather than discovering it mid-draft. If it does not, that is
a re-shape, not a blocker.

`uncertainties: deferred` — the contiguity-relaxation rules are a Planning-time design call, which
is a legitimate deferral: it is a product-shaped choice inside a known mechanism, not an unresolved
trust boundary.

**Verified before promoting, not assumed:** all eight DoR items are `met` or `deferred` with none
`open`, and every `blocked-by` link resolves to a **Done** ticket. Promoted as part of a sweep of
every fully-shaped Backlog ticket, on the owner's instruction.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — US-018: Best-available seat selection

Running **gateless per `config.gates: "autonomous"`** — gates 2, 3 and 4 are taken by the agent;
Gate 1 was the owner's (promoted 2026-08-17). Backend: **local tracker** (`config.tracker: "local"`).

**Blockers verified against the board, not the ticket text:** the single wired link is
`blocked-by TKT-80` and TKT-80 reads **Done**. Status re-read from `GET /board` before claiming —
the ticket really is in `Ready`, so no shaping was skipped.

**Branch:** `TKT-81-best-available-seats` off `origin/main`.

**Selection reason:** the owner asked for TKT-81 by key. It is the last unbuilt piece of the seated
story arc (TKT-80 seat claims → TKT-181 adjacency projection → TKT-182 the orphan rule → this), and
ADR-041 § Consequences already names it as the intended second reader of the projection it built.

### risk verdict — `risk:low` NOT claimed

Stated explicitly rather than left silent (TKT-190). This ticket is the opposite of low risk on
three of the label's own carve-outs:

- it writes on the **claim path under the pool row lock**, the platform's most contended
  transaction and the one ADR-010 exists to protect;
- it is a **concurrency** change by construction — AC3 is literally "parallel requests never
  double-assign";
- it will almost certainly touch **more than 5 files** (inventory store + handler + OpenAPI +
  generated types + tests, and possibly commerce).

The plan gate therefore applies in full (taken by the agent under autonomous mode, with the
cross-model critique unchanged).

### One thing checked at claim time, because Gate 1 asked for it

Gate 1's promotion note flagged that the ACs cite *"the map's adjacency/rank data (TKT-3 provides
both)"* while TKT-3 is still a Backlog epic, and asked the claimer to confirm the **rank** data
exists before Planning. **It does not.** Verified, not assumed:

- **Adjacency: exists.** `seat_claim_adjacency` (inventory migration `0011_seat_claim_adjacency.sql`,
  TKT-181) carries `(pool_id, seat_identity, left_identity, right_identity)`, pool-scoped, projected
  once at provisioning from the pool's immutable published seat-map version (ADR-041 Option 4).
  `services/inventory/internal/store/seat_claims.go` already reads it under the pool lock.
- **Rank: does not exist, anywhere.** `git grep -ni rank` across `services/catalog`,
  `services/inventory` and `docs/adr` returns only pricing/fee-resolution ranking
  (`scopeRank`, `channelSpecificity`, ADR-036/046/047). There is no seat desirability, quality,
  tier or preference datum in either service. What catalog *does* carry is
  `position` (`seat_maps` migration `0009`): a monotone ordinal on sections, rows and seats,
  which is an **ordering**, not a rank — it says which seat is next to which, not which is better.

Per Gate 1's own wording this is *"a re-shape, not a blocker"* — and the re-shape is small, so it is
recorded here rather than sent back to Backlog: **Planning will define best-available ordering over
the `position` ordinal that exists, and the plan will say so explicitly.** No seat-quality model is
invented in this ticket; if the owner later wants true rank (price tier, sightline, house scoring),
that is new data and a new ticket, and the selection comparator built here is where it would plug in.

Transitioning `Ready → Planning`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Execution plan — DRAFT

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna` via the codex companion** (`config.models.plan`), effort high,
read-only, against the real tree at `origin/main`. Posted verbatim below apart from the codex
session trailer. It has NOT yet been critiqued — `config.models.planReview` (`main-agent`) does
that next, and the binding plan is the `kind=plan-final` delta.

The brief it was given carried: the three ACs, the claim-time finding that **no seat rank data
exists** anywhere in the system, the ten governing ADRs re-resolved at claim time (ADR-010, 041,
005, 019, 022, 020, 029, 031, 017) with what each constrains *for this ticket*, the governing
tests (`check-generate` drift, contract validation, tier-of-mechanism, fixture-can-fail,
N-predicates-N-tests), the real code at the seam, and ten enumerated decisions it had to make and
defend.

---

# TKT-81 / US-018 execution plan

## Recommended decisions

Use a new public endpoint:

`POST /holds/seats/best-available`

Request:

```json
{
  "organizer_id": "...",
  "slot_id": "...",
  "seat_count": 2,
  "ticket_type_id": "...",
  "unit_amount": 3000,
  "currency": "EUR"
}
```

This preserves the existing `/holds/seats` contract for explicitly named seats and avoids an awkward request XOR. The route remains public, matching `registerRoutes` in [server.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/api/server.go:107).

Best available means:

- Select a free contiguous run within one row.
- Order candidates by the projected row key, then seat position.
- Use seat position for geometric order; never sort seat identities lexically.
- No seat-quality or desirability ranking is claimed because none exists.
- No cross-row or cross-section adjacency.
- No party splitting in this ticket. If no contiguous run of `N` exists, return `best_available_unavailable`.
- On orphan-prevention pools, reuse `orphanedSeats`; a selected run that would strand a seat is refused with existing `orphaned_seats`.
- `N` must be `1..MaxSeatsPerHold` (`50`).
- `N > 50`, zero, malformed, or missing values are `400`.
- No contiguous run or insufficient capacity is a deterministic `409 best_available_unavailable`.

Best-available is supported only when `inventory_pools.orphan_prevention_enabled = true`. Rule-off pools have no projection by design and fail closed rather than falling back to non-contiguous or identity-sorted selection. Decoupling the selection projection from the orphan flag should be a separate ticket.

## Idempotency

The best-available fingerprint must represent intent, not the eventual seats:

```text
best:<organizer>:<slot>:<ticket_type>:<seat_count>:<unit_amount>:<currency>
```

The lookup must happen after the pool lock and before selection. A same-key retry:

- returns the original claim and persisted selected seats;
- never selects a second run;
- returns `ErrIdempotency` if `seat_count` or any monetary term differs;
- returns the existing terminal/replay behavior for expired or released claims.

The fingerprint must include a mode prefix so a named-seat request and a best-available request cannot collide under one key.

## Projection and selection design

Add indexed ordering metadata to `seat_claim_adjacency`:

- `row_key`
- `position`

`position` is the catalog seat order within a row. `row_key` identifies the row. The existing adjacency edges remain authoritative for contiguity; the new columns make enumeration index-backed instead of requiring a recursive linked-list walk.

The selection query should be a package-level `const`, like `seatOccupancySeatsQuery`, so the index-plan test can EXPLAIN the exact SQL shipped.

Expected query shape:

1. Read projected seats for one pool through `(pool_id, row_key, position)`.
2. Determine live occupancy using the same liveness predicate as `seatOccupancySeatsQuery`.
3. Group free seats into contiguous runs by row and projected order.
4. Select the first run containing at least `N` seats.
5. Return seats in projected position order.
6. Run the existing orphan projection check before inserting the claim.

Work is one indexed pass over the finite projection for the pool, stopping at the first eligible run; worst case scans the pool when no run exists. It has no recursive CTE and no retry loop. The result is bounded by the provisioned map size and `MaxSeatsPerHold` output size.

The pool row lock remains first, followed by claim-row reads and writes, exactly as required by ADR-010. Selection and claim occur in the same transaction.

## Files to touch

Implementation:

- [0018_best_available_seat_order.sql](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/store/migrations/0018_best_available_seat_order.sql)
  - Add nullable `row_key` and `position`.
  - Backfill existing adjacency rows by walking each validated linked-list row.
  - Fail migration if any projection row cannot be assigned metadata.
  - Make both columns non-null.
  - Add the index on `(pool_id, row_key, position)`.
  - Add a guarded down migration; never silently remove metadata used by live pools.

- [seat_claims.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/store/seat_claims.go)
  - Add typed best-available errors, including `ErrBestAvailableUnavailable`.
  - Extend `SeatAdjacencyRow`.
  - Validate row metadata in `validateAdjacency`.
  - Include metadata in `ProvisionSeated`.
  - Add the package-level best-available selection query.
  - Add `CreateBestAvailableSeatHold`.
  - Reuse the existing pool-lock, expiry sweep, capacity accounting, idempotency, claim insert, history append, and `commitAvailability` flow.
  - Load persisted `claim_seats` on best-available replay rather than reconstructing seats from the request.

- [catalog.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/consumer/catalog.go:199)
  - Preserve row identity and seat position when deriving adjacency.
  - Continue deriving adjacency from catalog `position`, not identity labels or arithmetic.

- [consumer.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:195)
  - Forward the new adjacency metadata into `store.SeatAdjacencyRow`.
  - Do not change the domain event payload or schema number; metadata is derived during the existing schema-5 catalog lookup.

- [server.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/api/server.go:343)
  - Register `/holds/seats/best-available`.
  - Decode and validate `seat_count`.
  - Reuse the existing hold-then-pin flow.
  - Map `ErrBestAvailableUnavailable` to `409 best_available_unavailable`.
  - Preserve `orphaned_seats`, `pin_unavailable`, and pin-compensation semantics.

- [openapi.yaml](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/api/openapi.yaml:45)
  - Add the endpoint and `BestAvailableSeatHoldCreate`.
  - Add `best_available_unavailable` to the conflict-code enum.
  - Document that the response contains the selected `seats`, while the request contains only `seat_count`.

Generated outputs:

- [openapi_gen.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/api/openapi_gen.go)
- [inventory-api-types.gen.ts](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/src/lib/inventory-api-types.gen.ts)

Tests:

- New [best_available_smoke_test.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/store/best_available_smoke_test.go)
  - Real PostgreSQL, `//go:build smoke`.
  - Use `seededOrphanPool` from [seat_occupancy_smoke_test.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/store/seat_occupancy_smoke_test.go:819), extending its metadata and adding multi-row fixtures.
  - Add the required real-Postgres EXPLAIN test.

- [seat_occupancy_smoke_test.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/store/seat_occupancy_smoke_test.go)
  - Update valid `SeatAdjacencyRow` fixtures with row metadata.

- New [best_available_handler_smoke_test.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/api/best_available_handler_smoke_test.go)
  - Exercise response mapping, pinning, replay, projection refusal, and contract shape using the real store plus `recordingPinner`.

- [seat_pin_client_test.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/inventory/internal/consumer/seat_pin_client_test.go)
  - Assert that catalog-derived adjacency preserves row boundaries and position metadata.

- New [best_available_test.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/smoke/best_available_test.go)
  - End-to-end schema-5 publication, projection provisioning, best-available request, replay, and response contract validation.
  - This also satisfies the smoke operation-coverage gate for the new endpoint.

- New [ADR-061-best-available-seat-selection.md](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/docs/adr/ADR-061-best-available-seat-selection.md)
  - Record the endpoint, projection requirement, deterministic ordering, no-split policy, idempotency semantics, and atomic select-plus-claim rule.

Commerce files are intentionally out of scope. Commerce currently accepts named seats only at `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:733` and `:885`; TKT-81 should expose the inventory capability for the future picker without changing the reservation surface. TKT-35 can add commerce/storefront integration later.

## Definition of done

- Best-available requests accept `seat_count` from 1 through 50.
- Selection uses catalog-derived adjacency/order metadata, never identity lexical order.
- Selected seats are contiguous within one row.
- Selection, orphan validation, and claim insertion occur under the existing pool lock in one transaction.
- Same-key retries return the original selected seats and never allocate a second run.
- Rule-off or incomplete projections fail closed without writing claims.
- No splitting is performed.
- No orphan-prevention rule is bypassed.
- Contention produces no duplicate live seat claims, no oversell, no deadlock, and no retry loop.
- New route and conflict code pass OpenAPI runtime validation.
- Generated files are regenerated and committed before `make check`.
- `make check` passes.

## Test plan and failure mutation

| Test | Tier | What it proves | Deletion that must make it fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| First deterministic contiguous run | Store smoke / real PostgreSQL | Position order and row boundaries are honored | Delete the selection query, row partition, or `ORDER BY` |
| Identity-order trap | Store smoke | `A/1/10` does not sort before `A/1/2` geometrically | Replace position ordering with `seat_identity` ordering |
| Same-key replay | Store smoke | Retry returns the original seats | Move selection before idempotency lookup or omit mode/count from fingerprint |
| Changed count/terms | Store smoke | Same key cannot be reused for a different request | Remove fingerprint comparison |
| Rule-off pool | Store smoke/API smoke | No projection is treated differently from incomplete projection | Remove the `orphan_prevention_enabled` capability check |
| Incomplete projection | Store smoke | Enabled pools fail closed and write no claim | Delete `projectionGapsQuery` validation |
| Orphan-preserving selection | Store smoke | Existing ADR-041 rule remains active | Delete the call to `orphanedSeats` |
| N bounds and no-run refusal | Handler smoke | `MaxSeatsPerHold`, no-run, and insufficient-capacity behavior are explicit | Remove validation or refusal mapping |
| Index scope | Store smoke | The shipped selection query uses `(pool_id,row_key,position)` | Drop the new index or remove `pool_id` from the index condition |
| Blocked parallel claimants | Store smoke using `TestOrphanRuleHoldsUnderContention`’s blocker/`pg_blocking_pids` harness | Requests actually overlap, serialize, and complete without duplicates | Move selection before the pool lock or add an unbounded retry |
| Cross-service provisioning | `smoke/` | Schema-5 catalog geometry reaches inventory with metadata intact | Stop forwarding metadata in `catalog.go` or `consumer.go` |
| API contract coverage | `smoke/contract_validation_test.go` path | Request/response match OpenAPI | Change the spec without regeneration or change the handler shape |

AC3 belongs primarily in the real-Postgres store smoke tier because the mechanism is SQL and the pool row lock. `smoke/inventory_contention_test.go` is not sufficient for the load-bearing proof unless it provisions a rule-enabled seated pool; it may receive an additional end-to-end happy-path check, but the atomicity assertion belongs beside `CreateSeatHold`.

## Risks

- The indexed query is still O(pool seats) in the no-run case while holding the pool lock. This is bounded and non-recursive, but large seat maps may make rejected best-available requests expensive.
- Existing rule-enabled pools need migration backfill. The migration must fail rather than silently assign incorrect row metadata.
- Existing rule-off seated pools remain unsupported until a future projection-capability change. This is intentional but operationally significant.
- A strict FIFO guarantee cannot be inferred from PostgreSQL lock ordering. The test should measure bounded completion and allocation fairness, not promise request-arrival order.
- The endpoint returns a hold before catalog pinning, so it must retain the existing hold-then-pin compensation path exactly.

## Open decisions requiring owner confirmation

1. Confirm that “fair degradation” means bounded completion, no starvation in the contention harness, and deterministic allocation—not strict request-arrival FIFO.
2. Confirm that party splitting is deferred and unavailable when no contiguous run of `N` exists.
3. Confirm that TKT-81 supports only projection-enabled pools, with decoupling from `orphan_prevention_enabled` deferred.
4. Confirm the public conflict code name: recommended `best_available_unavailable`.
5. Confirm that arbitrary deterministic row ordering is acceptable in the absence of a seat-quality/rank model.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan -->
### Cross-model critique of the draft — by `main-agent` (`config.models.planReview`)

Drafter was `gpt-5.6-luna`; reviewer is the session model. The pair differs, so the cross-model
invariant holds. Adversarial pass, plus the pre-mortem lens. **Every file, symbol and test seam
the draft names was verified to exist at HEAD** (`git grep -n`) — results below.

## Seam verification — the draft did not hallucinate

| Named | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `services/inventory/internal/store/seat_claims.go` `CreateSeatHold`, `ProvisionSeated`, `validateAdjacency`, `orphanedSeats`, `MaxSeatsPerHold`, `projectionGapsQuery` | all exist |
| `internal/api/server.go:107` `registerRoutes`, `:116` `r.Post("/holds/seats", …)` | exist, route is public (not `internalOnly`) |
| `internal/consumer/catalog.go:199` `SeatMapAdjacency`, `:300-311` derivation | exists; row/position genuinely discarded at :300 |
| `seededOrphanPool` at `seat_occupancy_smoke_test.go:819` | exists, rule-enabled, one row of n seats |
| `TestOrphanRuleHoldsUnderContention` `pg_blocking_pids` harness `:962` | exists |
| `TestSeatOccupancyIsIndexScoped` `:357` EXPLAIN precedent | exists |
| migration `0018` next free | confirmed (0017 is the last) |
| `ADR-061` next free | confirmed (ADR-060 is the last) |
| `web/backoffice/src/lib/inventory-api-types.gen.ts` | exists |

Blast radius of extending `SeatAdjacencyRow` is genuinely small: `seat_claims.go` is the **only**
non-test reader of `seat_claim_adjacency` / `orphan_prevention_enabled`, and literal
`SeatAdjacencyRow{` fixtures appear in exactly two files (`consumer/consumer.go`,
`store/seat_occupancy_smoke_test.go`).

## Accepted without change

- **Option (b), project `row_key` + `position`, over (a) the recursive linked-list walk.** Correct,
  and for the reason ADR-041 already fixed: `orphanedSeatsQuery` was rewritten *because* an earlier
  version did O(map) work under the row lock that serialises every claimant on the performance. A
  recursive CTE per request re-introduces exactly that. The data is free — `catalog.go:289` already
  sorts by `Position` and then throws both the row key and the position away six lines later.
- **A separate endpoint over a request XOR on `SeatHoldCreate`.** Right call, and the draft's reason
  (avoiding the `minProperties`/`maxProperties` generator trick commerce was forced into) is the
  real one. A second reason it did not give and should have: `seat_identities` is
  `required` with `minItems: 1` today, and relaxing a required field is a **contract weakening** on
  a live public route that commerce already calls two ways.
- **The fingerprint covers intent (`mode:org:slot:type:count:amount:currency`), and the replay
  returns the PERSISTED seats.** This is the single most important correctness point in the ticket
  and the draft got it right, including the mode prefix that stops a named-seat and a
  best-available request colliding under one key. It also correctly puts the idempotency lookup
  **after the pool lock and before selection** — the only order in which a retry cannot select a
  second run.
- **No party splitting in this ticket**, refusing with a distinct code. Defensible: splitting is a
  product decision with no owner input available on a gateless run, and the reversible choice is to
  refuse rather than to ship a splitting policy nobody chose. See amendment 4 on the code name.
- **AC3 lives in the store smoke tier**, not `smoke/inventory_contention_test.go`. Correct per the
  repo's tier-of-mechanism rule: the mechanism is SQL under a row lock.
- **Commerce out of scope.** Consistent with the shaped scope (picker UI is TKT-35).
- **An ADR is warranted** (ADR-061). ADR-041 explicitly left selection open and named TKT-81 as the
  ticket that would decide it. That is a decision needing a record, not merely writing-down.

## Amendments — each a defect or a gap, not a preference

### A1 [blocking] The migration backfill is not derivable, and the draft asserts it is

The draft says the migration should *"backfill existing adjacency rows by walking each validated
linked-list row"*, then *"fail migration if any projection row cannot be assigned metadata"*, then
make both columns `NOT NULL`.

A `row_key` **cannot be recovered from the linked list**. Walking `left_identity IS NULL` heads
does yield the seats of one row in order, so `position` is derivable — but the row's *identity* is
not: it was never projected. Synthesising one (the head's identity, a hash, an ordinal) invents a
value that will **not match** what the consumer derives on the next re-provision, and since
`ProvisionSeated`'s adjacency insert is `ON CONFLICT (pool_id, seat_identity) DO NOTHING`, the two
would never reconcile — the projection would carry two incompatible row namings with nothing
reporting it.

Worse, a recursive walk in a migration is O(map) per pool across **every** rule-enabled pool, in a
migration that ADR-008's 30s bound applies to.

**Amendment.** Do not backfill by walking. Make `row_key` and `position` **nullable**, and treat a
NULL as *"this pool predates ordering metadata"* — a distinguishable state, exactly as
`orphan_prevention_enabled` distinguishes "rule off" from "projection missing". Best-available then
**fails closed** on such a pool with the same refusal it uses for a rule-off pool, and the repair
path is ADR-041's existing correction-wave machinery (re-emit → re-provision), not a migration.

This also removes the `NOT NULL` promotion, the failure mode where the migration aborts a deploy on
data it cannot interpret, and the 30s-bound risk.

### A2 [blocking] `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` means a re-provision never repairs the new columns

The draft's plan for existing pools is "the migration backfills them". With A1 that becomes "a
re-provision fills them" — and that path **does not work as written**, for a reason the code
comments already spell out for the *flag*:

`ProvisionSeated` (`seat_claims.go:411-416`) inserts adjacency row-at-a-time with
`ON CONFLICT(pool_id,seat_identity) DO NOTHING`. The rows already exist, so a re-provision of a
pre-existing pool is a **no-op on every adjacency row**. The pool would keep NULL `row_key`/
`position` for ever, and best-available would refuse it for ever, with the operator's correction
wave reporting success.

The file already contains the general form of this bug and its fix, three lines up, for
`orphan_prevention_enabled`: *"`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` is right for a REPLAY and wrong for an
UPGRADE, and the difference is invisible from here — both arrive as 'the pool already exists'."*

**Amendment.** The adjacency insert becomes
`ON CONFLICT (pool_id, seat_identity) DO UPDATE SET row_key = EXCLUDED.row_key, position = EXCLUDED.position`
— filling the ordering metadata on an upgrade — while **leaving `left_identity`/`right_identity`
untouched**. That asymmetry is deliberate and must be commented: the edges are the arbitration
substrate ADR-041 fail-closes on, and a `DO UPDATE` that rewrote them would let a later publication
silently redefine geometry a live claim was arbitrated against; the ordering columns are new,
additive, and read only by selection.

**This must be a test, not a comment.** Provision a rule-enabled pool without metadata, re-provision
it with metadata under a fresh event id, assert the rows now carry it *and* that the edges are
byte-identical. Deleting the `DO UPDATE` must make it red.

### A3 [blocking] "The index makes it bounded" is asserted, not argued — and the no-run case is O(pool) under the lock

The draft says the query is *"one indexed pass over the finite projection for the pool, stopping at
the first eligible run; worst case scans the pool when no run exists"*, and then lists that worst
case under Risks as *"bounded and non-recursive"*.

A sequential scan of every seat in a pool, while holding the row lock that serialises every claimant
on the performance, **is** the cost ADR-041 rejected. Calling it bounded because the map is finite
is not an argument — the map is exactly the bound ADR-041 refused. And the no-run case is not
exotic: it is what every request gets once the show is nearly sold out, which is precisely when
contention is highest. The plan cannot ship with its worst case unexamined on the hottest path.

Three things must be settled before coding, and the plan must state them:

1. **An explicit cap.** The scan reads at most `K` candidate seats per request (a `LIMIT` on the
   ordered scan, not a post-filter). A request that finds no run within `K` refuses. `K` is named
   in the plan, justified, and pinned by a test.
2. **The index must serve the ORDER BY, not just the filter.** `(pool_id, row_key, position)` gives
   an ordered index scan so the `LIMIT` actually stops early rather than sorting the whole pool
   first. The ADR-019 proof therefore has to assert **no `Sort` node and a `Limit` that terminates
   the scan**, not merely "an index was used". `TestSeatOccupancyIsIndexScoped:357` is the
   precedent and its seeding rationale (200 distinct pools, `ANALYZE`, blind plan) must be copied —
   a plan test on a handful of rows proves nothing because a seq scan is genuinely correct there.
3. **Say plainly what is given up.** With a cap, best-available is *"the best run within the first
   K seats in projected order"*, not *"the globally best run"*. That is an honest and defensible
   product answer; silently pretending it is global is not.

### A4 [blocking] The refusal code conflates two states a caller must distinguish

The draft maps three different situations onto one code, `best_available_unavailable`:
no contiguous run exists; aggregate capacity is insufficient; and (implicitly) the pool has no
usable projection.

The third is categorically different. "No run of 4 left" tells a buyer *try 2*; "this slot cannot
serve best-available at all" tells them *pick seats yourself*, and tells an operator *this pool
needs re-provisioning*. Collapsing them makes an operational defect look like a sellout — the exact
failure ADR-041 designed `orphan_prevention_enabled` to prevent when it insisted "rule off" and
"projection missing" must never look alike.

**Amendment.** Two codes:

- `best_available_unavailable` — the pool supports best-available and cannot satisfy this `N`
  right now (no run, or insufficient headroom). Retryable, and `N-1` may well succeed.
- `best_available_unsupported` — this pool has no ordering projection (rule-off, or provisioned
  before ADR-061). **Never** succeeds until the pool is re-provisioned. Deterministic, not a
  sellout.

Both are added to the conflict-code enum in `openapi.yaml`, with the distinction documented in the
enum description the way that file documents `channel_window_closed` vs a code-less capacity
refusal, and `presale_code_invalid`'s deliberate uniformity. Precedent is directly on point: TKT-238
added `channel_window_closed` for exactly this reason — *"the caller should wait for the window
rather than treat the channel as sold out."*

### A5 [important] Capacity, orphan and selection interact, and the draft leaves the order unstated

The draft says selection runs, then `orphanedSeats` is called on the result. It does not say what
happens when the selected run is refused by the orphan rule. Taking the first eligible run and then
refusing it produces a request that fails while a legal run existed further along — a
best-available that reports "unavailable" about a map with free contiguous seats.

**Amendment.** The plan must state the resolution and pin it with a test. The reversible, cheapest
correct answer: **make the selection orphan-aware rather than orphan-checked** — a run that leaves a
single free seat isolated at its edge is not eligible in the first place, decided in the same SQL
pass. `orphanedSeats` is then retained as the **fail-closed backstop** on the chosen set (it also
runs `projectionGapsQuery`, which is the incomplete-projection guard the draft depends on), and the
test asserts a fixture where the naive first-run choice would be refused and the correct choice is
the second run. Without that test the two behave identically on every fixture and the distinction
is unfalsifiable.

Separately: state explicitly that the **aggregate capacity ceiling** (`confirmed + held + N > limit`
→ `ErrUnavailable`) is evaluated exactly where `CreateSeatHold` evaluates it — before selection, not
after — so a drained pool refuses without paying for a scan.

### A6 [important] Two of the draft's mutation-test entries cannot fail as written

The repo's own rule: *before trusting a green test, ask whether its fixture can reach the state
that would fail.* Two rows of the draft's table do not survive it.

- *"Rule-off pool → deletion: remove the `orphan_prevention_enabled` capability check."* Under A1
  the capability is **NULL ordering metadata**, not the flag. A test written against the flag stays
  green with the metadata check deleted, and vice versa. These are two predicates and, per the
  repo's N-predicates-N-tests rule, they need two tests, each passing the other's precondition:
  a rule-**on** pool with NULL metadata (must refuse `best_available_unsupported`), and — if the
  design keeps requiring the flag — a rule-off pool **with** metadata.
- *"Index scope → deletion: drop the new index."* Dropping an index on a small fixture changes
  nothing, because a seq scan was already correct. Per A3 this test only means something with the
  200-pool `ANALYZE`d seeding, and its assertion must be no-`Sort` + early-terminating `Limit`.

Also add the mutation the table omits: **delete the `DO UPDATE` from A2** and assert the upgrade
test goes red.

### A7 [minor] Not every fixture needs metadata

The draft says `seat_occupancy_smoke_test.go` fixtures must be updated with row metadata. Under A1
the columns are nullable and the existing orphan-rule tests do not read them, so the correct action
is to update **only** `seededOrphanPool` (parameterised, or a sibling helper that adds metadata) and
leave the ADR-041 fixtures alone. Touching them would be churn in tests that pin a shipped rule, and
per the repo's rule a test whose fake/fixture moves with the mechanism silently becomes an assertion
that the old behaviour is correct.

## Pre-mortem — it is three months on and this shipped badly. What happened?

1. **Every seated pool refuses best-available in production.** Ordering metadata is written only by
   a re-provision, and nobody ran the correction wave — or they ran it and A2's `DO NOTHING` ate it.
   *Mitigated by:* A2's `DO UPDATE` + its upgrade test, A4's distinguishable `unsupported` code, and
   an explicit operator note in the ADR saying re-provisioning is the enablement step.
2. **An on-sale stalls.** The show is 95% sold, every best-available request scans the whole map
   under the pool lock, and claim latency for *named-seat* buyers collapses with it — the blast
   radius is not confined to the feature. *Mitigated by:* A3's cap and the ordered-index proof.
3. **A retry double-allocates.** A client retries a timed-out best-available with the same key and
   gets a second run, quietly selling twice the seats. *Mitigated by:* the draft's own fingerprint
   design (accepted) plus a test that asserts the replay returns the **persisted** seats and no
   second `claims` row appears.
4. **Support cannot tell a sellout from a broken pool** because both answered
   `best_available_unavailable`. *Mitigated by:* A4.
5. **The contiguity test proved nothing.** The fixture was one row where every free run was
   equivalent, so a wrong `ORDER BY` passed. *Mitigated by:* the identity-order trap the draft
   already lists (`A/1/10` vs `A/1/2` — good), plus A5's two-run fixture where the first eligible
   run is the wrong answer.

## Verdict

**Accept with amendments A1–A7.** The draft's core judgement is right on the two decisions that
mattered most — project the ordering data rather than chase the linked list, and fingerprint the
*intent* while replaying the *persisted seats* — and its seams are real. A1–A4 are blocking: two are
correctness defects on the upgrade path, one is an unexamined worst case on the platform's hottest
lock, and one is an operational-signal collapse with direct precedent against it. A5–A7 close gaps
that would otherwise produce green tests about nothing.
